name: Citizenship by Descent (Section 5(1))

qualifying_event.description: A person with a Barbadian parent may apply for Barbadian citizenship under Section 5(1) of the Barbados citizenship framework, via the Immigration Department.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Applicant's birth certificate; parent's birth certificate and proof of the parent's Barbados citizenship; parent's marriage certificate.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires at least one parent to be a Barbadian citizen, proven via the parent's birth certificate and proof of Barbadian citizenship, plus the parents' marriage certificate.

evidence_required.document: Parent's birth certificate and proof of Barbados citizenship
Medical certificate (form varies by applicant age)

sources.title: Barbados Immigration Department -- Barbadian Citizenship: by descent (Section 5(1)), by marriage, by registration/naturalisation, and Section 3(2), with required documents and fees

notes: NEW ROUTE, filling a gap flagged in bb_naturalisation.json's notes: that earlier pass extracted the Barbados Citizenship Act, Cap. 186 (Second Schedule) from barbadoslawcourts.gov.bb and found NO general descent-based citizenship provision, only a narrow diplomatic/consular exception -- and explicitly flagged this as a surprising, likely-outdated gap. This route resolves that gap using the Immigration Department's OWN citizenship page (immigration.gov.bb), a different tier-1 source, which describes a Section 5(1) descent ground plainly and without a residence requirement. The section numbering here (3, 3(3), 3A(1)(b), 4(3), 5(1), 6) does not match the Second Schedule numbering bb_naturalisation cited, confirming the earlier suspicion that the Cap. 186 text as consolidated at barbadoslawcourts.gov.bb may be out of date relative to a subsequent amendment -- this is flagged, not silently reconciled. No specific residence period is stated for this ground in the source. dual_citizenship_allowed left null: not independently confirmed at tier-1 in this pass, consistent with bb_naturalisation's own unresolved flag on this point.
